headline: A 2020 law let veterans keep receiving education benefits, including housing stipends, for classes moved online because of emergencies such as COVID-19, through December 21, 2020.
what_it_does: The law tells the Department of Veterans Affairs to treat school programs that switched to distance learning because of an emergency or health situation the same way it treats in-person programs. This keeps education assistance flowing for those students. The assistance covers monthly housing stipends or subsistence allowances. The special treatment runs through December 21, 2020.

who_it_affects.group: Veterans and eligible family members using VA education benefits
who_it_affects.how: They can keep receiving education payments, including housing stipends, for programs that moved to online classes because of an emergency.

who_it_affects.group: Schools offering programs approved for VA education benefits
who_it_affects.how: Programs that switched to distance learning during the emergency can still count as eligible for VA payments through the deadline.

when_it_takes_effect: Enacted March 21, 2020; the education assistance provision applies through December 21, 2020.
